title: Introduction to MAIHDA
text: MAIHDA package provides specialized tools conducting Multilevel Analysis Individual Heterogeneity Discriminatory Accuracy. modern epidemiological approach highly effective investigating intersectional health inequalities understanding joint social categories (e.g., Race x Gender x Education) influence individual outcomes. utilizing multilevel mixed-effects models (via lme4 brms), MAIHDA allows researchers : 1. Automatically construct intersectional strata. 2. Estimate -stratum variance Variance Partition Coefficients (VPC). 3. Evaluate Proportional Change Variance (PCV) understand much inequalities driven additive main effects versus unique intersectional effects. 4. Launch interactive Shiny Dashboard code-free analysis.

title: Introduction to MAIHDA
text: package includes pedagogical subset National Health Nutrition Examination Survey (maihda_health_data). use examine Body Mass Index (BMI) varies across intersectional demographic groups.

what: Step 1 & 2: Create Intersectional Strata and Fit a Null MAIHDA Model
title: Introduction to MAIHDA
text: Use fit_maihda() combine multiple social categories directly random effect formula. Providing variables random effect combined + allows function automatically build intersectional strata fly fit multilevel model. Interpretation: resulting Variance Partition Coefficient (VPC ICC) tells us percentage total variance BMI population lies intersectional social groups, rather just within .
code: library(MAIHDA)  # Load the built-in NHANES dataset data("maihda_health_data")  # Fit the initial Null model with auto-generated strata model_null <- fit_maihda(   BMI ~ 1 + (1 | Gender:Race:Education),   data = maihda_health_data,   engine = "lme4" )  # Summarize the variance components (VPC) summary_null <- summary(model_null) print(summary_null)

what: Step 3: Evaluate Proportional Change in Variance (PCV)
title: Introduction to MAIHDA
text: understand intersectional inequalities simply sum parts (additive), evaluate much variance explained adding main-effects model. variance drops significantly (High PCV), inequalities largely explained additive characteristics. variance remains even increases (Negative PCV), signifies strong, unique intersectional interactions explained away simple main effects.
code: # Fit an adjusted model model_adj <- fit_maihda(   BMI ~ Age + Gender + Race + Education + Poverty + (1 | Gender:Race:Education),   data = maihda_health_data )  # Calculate PCV with Parametric Bootstrap Confidence Intervals pcv_result <- calculate_pvc(model_null, model_adj, bootstrap = TRUE, n_boot = 500) print(pcv_result)

title: Introduction to MAIHDA
text: Often, researchers want know exactly variable explained variance. Use stepwise_pcv() function add covariates one--one track variance dynamically. Negative step PCVs table highlight “unmasking” suppression effects: adding variable caused intersectional groups push apart mathematically, revealing hidden structural inequalities.
code: # Run a stepwise variance decomposition (using the auto-generated strata from model_null) stepwise_results <- stepwise_pcv(   data = model_null$data,   outcome = "BMI",   vars = c("Age", "Gender", "Race", "Education", "Poverty") )  print(stepwise_results)

title: Calculate Proportional Change in Between-Stratum Variance (PVC) — calculate_pvc
text: PVC interpreted proportional reduction (increase negative) -stratum variance moving model1 model2. positive PVC indicates model2 explains -stratum variance present model1, negative PVC suggests model2 unexplained -stratum variance. bootstrap = TRUE, function resamples data replacement refits models bootstrap sample obtain confidence intervals PVC estimate.

title: Calculate Proportional Change in Between-Stratum Variance (PVC) — calculate_pvc
code: # \donttest{ # Create strata and fit two models strata_result <- make_strata(maihda_sim_data, c("gender", "race")) model1 <- fit_maihda(health_outcome ~ age + (1 | stratum), data = strata_result$data) #> Warning: the ‘findbars’ function has moved to the reformulas package. Please update your imports, or ask an upstream package maintainer to do so. #> This warning is displayed once per session. model2 <- fit_maihda(health_outcome ~ age + gender + (1 | stratum), data = strata_result$data)  # Calculate PVC without bootstrap pvc_result <- calculate_pvc(model1, model2) print(pvc_result$pvc) #> [1] -0.1626748  # Calculate PVC with bootstrap CI # pvc_boot <- calculate_pvc(model1, model2, bootstrap = TRUE, n_boot = 500) # print(pvc_boot) # }

Added plot_risk_vs_effect() function create quadrant scatterplot comparing overall marginal predicted risk pure intersectional effects. Added plot_effect_decomposition() function visually decompose total deviation overall mean additive intersectional components. Replaced redundant “caterpillar” plot “predicted” plot plot() interactive dashboard. Added automatic tertile binning (via autobin parameter) numeric grouping variables 10 unique values make_strata(). Added fully-featured interactive Shiny Dashboard (via run_maihda_app()) visual data exploration, model fitting, performance visualization. Improved bootstrap methods efficient confidence interval estimation. Added missing documentation block maihda_sim_data dataset resolve R CMD check warnings. Updated test suite setup: tests/testthat.R modified correctly use test_check("MAIHDA") instead shinytest2. Added importFrom(stats, .formula) stepwise_pcv function prevent undefined warnings. Updated introduction.Rmd vignette: added standard CRAN installation instructions, improved text clarity.
